body: **2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — set the readiness gate as a driver-only bound: a verified `viola send` waits up to `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s) for the input box and is then refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed. A human key during that wait goes to the child, takes the wheel at once, and the send is refused `human-typing`. It added the outer-PTY case `send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins`, sequenced on the `channel-request` line and the `wheel` record and never on a timer. Its stated limit is that it cannot tell `send`'s first wheel read from its second, so the proof sits at the unit tier. This is the closest precedent for item 3, the readiness-gate turn race: a turn starting inside the same gate window must not receive the text. Rows decision/human-key-takes-the-wheel and decision/time-bounds-never-on-human carry this rule. The new race test should follow the same record-sequenced, unit-tier-for-ordering pattern (decision/boundary-tests-sequenced-on-records).

**2026-10-04-the-wheel** — set the tui wheel boundary: a closed non-editing list (focus reports, mouse reports, terminal replies), where every other byte counts as editing and takes the wheel. The wheel is probed by exit codes, 13 for driver and 10 for human. The rule that errors only ever favour the human (F-W2/F-W3) bounds item 1: the trim-tolerant match may only stop a driver's own submitted prompt from being read as human input. A human's own prompt must still take the wheel. Rows decision/stdin-classifier-non-editing-list, decision/non-editing-sequences, contract/cli-exit-codes/10.

**2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive** — extended the closed non-editing list by exact grammar: a sequence one field or one prefix away from a listed shape still counts as typing. It also recorded the first live takeover reading (`wheel{human, human-input}`, the next driver `send` exited 10). Item 1 has the same precedent: the match tolerates exactly the CLI's trim and nothing more, and any other differing byte stays human (row decision/stdin-classifier-non-editing-list). Live readings are supplemental and never gating (decision/live-readings-never-gate).

**2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola** — recorded the second live takeover reading on claude 2.1.296: a human key wrote `wheel{holder:"human",cause:"human-input"}`, the next driver `send` exited 10 `human-typing` with no `send-issued`, and `viola release` wrote `wheel{holder:"driver",cause:"release"}`. The scope's measured premise is the same mechanism firing falsely: a trimmed driver send was read as `origin: human`, and every later send was refused until a `release`. The fix must keep this genuine-takeover reading intact (critical path decision/critical-path-human-takes-wheel).

**2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row** — added the confirm windows: `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` 10 s, and `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` 40 s for `/compact` on a verified CLI. A typed send left unconfirmed is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`, and the bound falls on the driver only. Today a trimmed send misses its match and lands on this unconfirmed path (exit 13 although the skill ran). Item 1 must confirm it inside the same window without moving the window or making it bind a human (rows contract/send-refusal/no-prompt-submitted, decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver).

**2026-11-13-verify-readiness-on-the-input-box** — `~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing`: the vendor screen is parsed only for compiled signatures, and the input box's prompt row only for its opening char, never the text after it (a ratified boundary widening, PROVISIONAL card confirm). This is a trap for items 1 and 3: the trim match and the gate race fix must not read the submitted prompt text off the rendered screen. The match should compare the hook's `prompt` payload against the in-flight slot (`SendSlot::claim`), and the gate's settled-input-box predicate must keep its signature-only reading.

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — added the tui passthrough clause for after a contained vt100 feed panic. The driver's `send` is refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` (exit 13), a typed human key still reaches the child, and no viola literal reaches the outer terminal (`tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs`). The gate changes in item 3 touch this same `input-not-ready` path, so this clause must keep holding (row contract/tui-passthrough/after-feed-panic).

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** (`--json`'s one document and its exit-2 exception) — `viola send`'s exit-2 path writes the fixed `UNUSABLE_TEXT` line to stderr whatever `--json` says, with no document (named in `NOT_ERROR_BODIES`, `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`). The same chunk set the clean `--json` failure documents (`cli_error_documents_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text`). Item 2's "validated as received, never stripped" must keep the send-text refusals on these shapes: `control-character` and `empty-text` stay `not-delivered` refusals in the standard layout, and nothing new joins the exit-2 exception (rows contract/cli-json-failure/send-answer-exit-2, contract/cli-refusal/json, decision/json-failure-documents-are-clean).

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** (the cli checks on std::process::Command and literal pins; the §8 verification lines pinned by literal) — the refusal layout (`unable <reason> <detail>` plus a final `hint:`), the typed exit codes (10–14, 20, 21) and a hint-free `--json` are held by literal asserts over `std::process::Command`. Every fixed CLI string is pinned by literal, so a copy change fails CI on purpose. Any refusal or hint this chunk adds or touches (`turn-running`, `control-character`, `human-typing`) must take these literal pins (rows decision/refusal-layout-literal-pins, decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned, decision/cli-a11y-by-literal-tests).

Any outer-PTY case this chunk adds for the race uses that pin as-is (rows decision/tui-boundary-driver-pin, decision/portable-pty-outer-pty-driver).

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** (the tui boundary on openpty alone; the a11y cases' CI home) — the TUI is hosted in openpty only, and the F-W3 Windows arm is retired. Each of the three boundary clauses (zero viola bytes, keystrokes never blocked, focus/mouse/resize never move the wheel) is its own nextest case on `ubuntu-latest`, inside the `coverage` suite gated by `gate --require coverage,doctest`. New boundary or race cases in this chunk land there (rows decision/tui-boundary-assertions-only, decision/zero-viola-bytes-on-the-terminal, decision/wheel-ignores-terminal-events).

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** — `~ contract/cli-exit-codes/11`: exit 11 is retired and never reused. `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` and `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` drop the budget pause. Precedent: a send refusal and its exit code are kept closed, so a `turn-running` refusal for item 3 must reuse an existing code (not exit 11). Any new bound must join these time-bound rows as driver-only.

**2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed** — `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` and `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver`: these set the current list of time bounds (wait timeout and cap, dialog hold, send readiness gate, confirm windows, agents read). Item 3's gate and turn handling must stay inside this list, or extend it explicitly, with the bound on the driver only.

**2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary** — the CLI output-discipline invariants (P4, P6) held in crate tests are covered by the epoch-boundary mutation audit (`run --mutants`), not by a per-chunk gate. This is consistent with the scope's "no mutation run" boundary (row decision/mutation-audit-covers-crate-invariants). New slot and relabel unit tests are audited at Epoch 3's boundary.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** — a passed `viola revive` enters the same TUI passthrough boundary as `viola run`, and the keystroke ban covers its starts. The match, relabel and gate changes apply to sends into revived starts too, under the same wheel and zero-viola-bytes clauses (rows decision/human-keystrokes-never-blocked, contract/tui-passthrough/own-bytes).

body: The confirmed send and readback critical path: a driver send whose prompt the CLI trims ends ok, its readback reads origin driver, and a later driver send is not refused for the wheel.
The human takes the wheel critical path: a human's own prompt, or a prompt differing from the send in any byte other than the trimmed whitespace, still takes the wheel as today.

C0/C1 control characters in the driver's text: a C0 other than LF, CR or TAB, DEL or C1 is refused with the code word control-character, never stripped or escaped away; the CR LF and trailing CR/LF rules of the typed text stay as they are.

The viola send refusals and outcomes the chunk reaches: not-delivered with control-character, empty-text, turn-running for the readiness-gate race, input-not-ready and no-prompt-submitted — each as code word beside unable, with its exit code (13 for not-delivered) and its hint, on the human output and under --json.

Send refused while the human types and the readiness gate: the settled-input-box predicate still guards the paste, and a turn starting inside the gate's window refuses or defers the send rather than typing into a running turn.

The single vendor-content boundary: the rule naming what the claude CLI trims lives in the claude agent crate and is consumed by the send path as a normalised predicate; no claude shape in the wrapper's send code.
Live readings never gate: the trim's tolerance stands on the recorded fixtures and the fake agent, not on a live claude start; a live reading, if one is ever asked for, gates nothing.
The fake agent and its scripts: it must submit a trimmed prompt or start a turn inside the readiness gate's window, so the tests reproduce the CLI's behaviour without inspecting claude content.

Boundary tests sequenced on records: the race test orders the turn start and the send on recorded events, not on sleeps; it is deterministic, takes a bound on every channel or thread wait and cannot hang past a failure.
Time bounds fall on the driver only: the readiness gate's wait and any deferral until the turn ends bound the driver's send, never the human's keystrokes.
Human keystrokes never blocked: closing the race moves nothing onto the human's input; the human's typing still reaches the child while a send waits.
Fixed CLI strings pinned by literal: the refusal code words and the CLI send / MCP send outcome lines the chunk's tests read are pinned by their literal, as they already read the wrapper's reply.
Zero viola bytes on the terminal: the send's text is typed into the child as received, and the chunk adds no viola byte to the human's terminal.

The wheel on a matched trimmed send stays with the driver and a later driver send is not refused for the wheel; a human's own prompt still takes the wheel (human prompt confirms the wheel take, byte-source wheel claim, wheel decided in wrapper memory, the human always wins the wheel).
Every send confirmed after the fact; unconfirmed delivery reported not-delivered — the trimmed send must now confirm ok instead of exiting not-delivered (no-prompt-submitted, unconfirmable).
Paste text validation as received: control characters (C0 other than LF/CR/TAB, DEL, C1) refused not-delivered with the control-character detail, never stripped.

Typed text normalisation unchanged: CR LF and CR become one LF, trailing CR and LF not typed, send never types a trailing newline; no other whitespace removed before typing; send text line-ending rules.
An empty typed text stays the empty-text refusal (paste text empty, not-delivered empty-text detail); whether a text made only of CLI-trimmed whitespace needs its own decision is left to P3 and P4.

Claude shapes isolated in one crate: the trim rule lives in the Claude agent crate, which does no file I/O, and the root bin consumes it only as a normalised predicate (claude shapes in one crate, root bin consumes only normalised events, claude-first with no adapter trait).

The trim is an undocumented claude CLI behaviour: whether its tolerance stands on a capability-ledger row with a viola verify probe, on the recorded fixtures, or on a closed rule needing no row (capability ledger gate, per-behaviour CLI capability ledger, no probe for unrelied shapes) is read at P3 and decided at P4.

The readiness-gate turn race: a turn that starts while a send waits on the vt100 pre-send readiness gate never receives the text; the send is refused turn-running or typed only once that turn ended (a send mid-turn is refused, never queued).
The pre-send readiness gate itself: its settled-input-box predicate, compiled gate timings, the paste-hint wait, the send time bound, and the atomic bracketed-paste send the race window sits between.
Send refusals keep a closed set of details and the first-refusal-only order; a turn-running refusal from the gate window uses the existing refusal reason and its send-refused event data.
The wrapper's send records (send-issued, send-confirmed, send-refused appends) and the paste failing after send-issued stay ordered and log-only.
The CLI send and MCP send outcomes change only as they already read the wrapper's reply (CLI exit codes 0 and 13, MCP send result and refusal).

The fake agent (viola-fake-agent and its scripts) gains the means to submit a trimmed prompt and to start a turn inside the gate's window, through the fake-agent test seams, never read by the product.

No live claude start: tests run against the fake agent and the recorded payloads; real CLI probes only locally, and a live start, if the trim's shape needs one, is named and asked for before the review card.
A test that waits on a channel or a thread takes a bound and cannot hang past a failure (root test waits share one bound, nothing polls the channel).
Upstream prompt text from the hook payload is untrusted content, parsed tolerantly; the match compares it without trusting or rendering it.
The local-command classification keeps reading the exact typed text, not a trimmed one.

body: A prompt send whose text the CLI submits with whitespace trimmed ends as a confirmed prompt send. The send readback and the viola send readback mirror read back the driver's text, never unconfirmable or unable, and the send exits 0 instead of 13 not-delivered.

Confirmation still comes only from the matched prompt-submitted line, never before it. The relaxed match must not let a send announce success optimistically or claim a prompt that differs in any byte other than the trimmed whitespace.

On a trim-tolerant match the wheel stays with the driver. The flight-progress strip's WHEEL field and any wheel shown as words read the driver, not the human or human-input, and a later driver send is not refused for the wheel. A human's own unmatched prompt still takes the wheel.
The refusal not-delivered with control-character still applies to a text holding a C0 other than LF, CR or TAB, a DEL or a C1. Its fixed refusal line and its hint are unchanged.

A text that is empty after the typed-text rule is still refused not-delivered with empty-text, with that refusal's hint. Whether a text made only of trimmable whitespace needs its own outcome is left to P3 and P4.

A turn starting while a send waits on the readiness gate ends that send as not-delivered with turn-running, carrying the turn-running refusal hint, or the text is typed only after that turn ends. The input-not-ready and no-prompt-submitted outcomes keep their meanings.
CLI exit codes for send: exit 0 on a confirmed send, exit 13 not-delivered only where the text was truly not delivered, with stdout carrying data and stderr carrying the refusal line and its hint.

The CLI send and MCP send outcomes change only through the wrapper's reply they already read. Peer reply screening of refusal code words and the --json result document keep their shape, with no new code word unless P4 decides one.
Claude-specific knowledge of what the CLI trims lives only in the claude agent crate and reaches the send path as a normalised predicate. The wrapper's send path names no claude shape of its own.

The trim is undocumented claude CLI behaviour. Whether the tolerance stands on a capability-ledger row with a viola verify probe, on the recorded fixtures or on a closed rule is decided at P4, and the CLI verification state of verified or unverified-cli applies as it already does to sends.
Hints and errors from the send path quote no text and name no internals. No hint names viola release, even though the old mismatch could only be cleared by a release.
Every test that waits on a channel or a thread is bounded and cannot hang past a failure. The race test drives the fake agent to start a turn inside the gate's window.

The match tolerates exactly the whitespace the CLI trims: a submitted prompt differing in any other byte still claims nothing and is read as the human's, as today.

The wheel after a trimmed-but-matched send stays with the driver, and a later driver send is not refused for the wheel; a human's own prompt still takes the wheel (no release needed for the matched case).

The driver's text is validated as received: a C0 other than LF/CR/TAB, DEL or C1 is refused not-delivered with cause control-character, never removed; the CLI and the MCP wrapper keep repeating that refusal as today.
The typed text keeps today's rules (CR LF and CR as one LF, trailing CR and LF not typed) and nothing else is taken off; an empty typed text stays the empty-text refusal.

A send waiting on the readiness gate when a turn starts is refused with cause turn-running or typed only once that turn ends; the turn-running refusal reaches viola send and MCP send through their existing refusal line, exit code, hint and --json forms.
The readiness gate's own outcome (the input-not-ready cause and its hint) keeps its existing form; only the race window between the turn rung check and the paste is closed.

The CLI send and MCP send outcomes change only as they already read the wrapper's reply: the send --json typed document, the readback mirror line, the word column and the exit codes keep their shapes; no new outcome word or cause is added.
turn-ended stays not a send outcome: a send typed after the racing turn ends reports its own outcome, not the turn's end.
Claude shapes live only in the Claude agent crate: the rule naming what the CLI trims is stated there and the send path consumes it as a normalised predicate, naming no CLI byte itself.
The local-command list still reads the exact typed text: the read-back for /clear and /compact and their post-conditions are unchanged by the trim tolerance.

Tests stand on the fake agent and the recorded payloads: the fake agent submits a trimmed prompt or starts a turn inside the gate's window; any test waiting on a channel or thread takes a bound and cannot hang past a failure.
No live claude start is planned without asking first; no mutation run; every control fires with a timeout of 120 s or less on an entry filtered to the guard's own cases.

body: The driver send confirmation: a prompt-submitted payload whose prompt equals the typed text up to the whitespace the CLI trims is confirmed as the driver's own — origin driver, send ok, exit 0, the send-confirmed log line — and any other byte difference still claims nothing.

The send confirmation rule changes from an exact normalised match to a match tolerant of exactly the CLI's trim; the rule's own tests must show both the tolerated trim and a one-byte non-whitespace difference left unmatched.

The wheel after a trimmed driver send stays with the driver: no wheel human-input record, no human-typing refusal of a later driver send, no release needed; a genuinely human prompt still takes the wheel.

The send result outcomes: a trimmed send no longer exits 13 not-delivered / no-prompt-submitted; the CLI send --json document, the human-mode confirmed line and the MCP send ok result read the wrapper's reply as they already do.

Sent text validated as received at client and wrapper: a C0 other than LF, CR and TAB, DEL or C1 is refused not-delivered / control-character, never removed; the trimmable whitespace is not stripped before validation or typing.

The typed text keeps its rules (CR LF and CR as one LF, trailing CR and LF not typed, multi-line text one prompt, the typed framing); nothing else is taken off, and an empty typed text is refused empty-text before the wheel is read.

The readiness gate (settled input box, GATE_MAX_WAIT) and the send refusal order: a turn starting during the gate wait yields a turn-running refusal or a paste only after turn-ended — never text typed into the running turn.
The send event records: send-issued, send-confirmed and send-refused lines and the prompt-submitted event of the event log, with their corr fields, for a trimmed send and for the race.
Claude shapes only in the claude agent crate: the rule naming what the CLI trims lives there and the send path consumes it as a normalised predicate, never a claude literal in the send path.

Undocumented CLI behaviour: whether the trim tolerance stands on a capability-ledger row with a viola verify probe, on the recorded fixtures, or on a closed rule is the plan's to read; the recorded claude fixtures per CLI version and their replay are the evidence read.

The fake agent held to the recorded fixtures: a trimmed-prompt submission and a turn started inside the gate's window are added through its argv-only options, turn scripts, control-file gated steps and receipts, matching what the recordings show.

Race and match tests are E2E over the fake agent with real PTY and real filesystem, waits keyed on logged events, no sleeps or retries, each wait on a channel or thread bounded so none hangs past a failure, and the stamped-home kill lines respected.
Unit cases for the match and the trim predicate are table-driven inline unit tests with literal oracles, with property tests over the parser-like predicate where the plan asks it.
No live claude start and no mutation run in this chunk: real claude stays local-only and outside CI, and any guard control fires with a bounded timeout on the guard's own filtered cases.
Send confirmation window expiry and the unconfirmable local-command outcome stay intact for a send that is not matched; the local-command list still matches the exact typed text.
